_help: Per-skin fixes the model can't learn. Key = skin name (e.g. cookfemale1_b), outfit name (e.g. cookfemale1, applies to all its variants) or * (every skin). grey: colours (hex) to grey as skin; grey_area: [x0, y0, x1, y1] pixel boxes (inclusive) to grey as skin; keep: colours never to grey; untouched: colours never changed at all, neither greyed nor toned as hair (jewellery); keep_area: [x0, y0, x1, y1] pixel boxes (inclusive) never to change; hair_colours: colours (hex) always toned as hair, never greyed; hair_area: [x0, y0, x1, y1] pixel boxes (inclusive) always toned as hair; hair_hue: [lo, hi] CIELAB hue degrees hair must be in (brown is about 20-100), so a hat or hood of another colour isn't toned; hair: false to skip hair toning (a grey or white hood is found by itself: see hood_hair); dark_hair_rule: false when greyed dark areas on the head are really skin (e.g. shaved sides); hand: false to ignore your pass-1 edit for this skin and let the model decide; ears: true / false / "left" / "right" to force where add_ears.py paints elf ears; fill: [x, y] pixels to paint over with the median of their neighbours (e.g. a stray dot in the original); ash: colours (hex) to give the grey skin's blue-grey undertone at their own lightness, without greying them as skin; tint: {target colour: [colours]} to recolour those original colours to the target, keeping their shading; darken_area: [x0, y0, x1, y1, amount] boxes (inclusive) to darken by that much L* (0-100 lightness), e.g. brows; desat: {colour: factor} to take colour out of those pixels at the end (0 = grey, 0.5 = half as colourful); skin_darker: L* (0-100 lightness) to darken the grey skin by (negative lightens); soft_shadows: true (or how far below the median skin, in L*, to start) to keep the deepest skin shadows dark grey instead of near-black; torso_bottom: "keep" to keep the torso's own underside instead of the leg tops' texture (the default), "original" to put back the original texture's underside (both layers, not greyed), or "left" / "right" to use just that leg's top for both halves; face_paint: [{colour, area: [[x0, y0, x1, y1]], strength}] to grey those pixels as skin and then move their colour strength (0-1) of the way to the paint colour, keeping the grey shading, so face paint sits on the ash undertone. slim_arms: false to keep arms painted 4 px wide as they are instead of re-laying them onto a 3 px arm model; tint_area: [{colour, area: [[x0, y0, x1, y1]], strength}] to move those pixels' colour strength (0-1) of the way to the colour, keeping their lightness and without greying them (e.g. a slight purple on grey cloth). hair_tone: [saturation, value, contrast] factors to tone this skin's hair with instead of the usual pick (e.g. [0.55, 0.75, 1.0] is the default for brown hair; raise saturation to desaturate less); hair_only_area: [x0, y0, x1, y1] pixel boxes (inclusive) hair toning is limited to, for hair that is only on part of the texture (chainmail, clothes elsewhere get mistaken for it); hair_darker: L* (0-100 lightness) to darken the toned hair by (negative lightens); copy_area: [[src_x, src_y, w, h, dst_x, dst_y]] blocks to paint over other parts of the texture (after recolouring, before the torso underside takes the leg tops), e.g. a leg top from the pants overlay front or from the torso's own underside. borrow_area: [[skin, src_x, src_y, w, h, dst_x, dst_y]] blocks pasted from another skin's original before recolouring and greyed as skin, e.g. a bare hand's underside where this skin only has a glove. hair_tint: {colour, strength} to move the toned hair's colour that far (0-1) towards the colour, keeping its lightness (e.g. slightly redder hair). brow_style: "hair" (default for blonde hair) to paint the brows in the toned hair's colour, "default" to darken and mute their own colour.
